item.title: Rallies continue outside Senator Capito's Morgantown office, despite arrests
item.description: Two weeks ago, six members of the clergy were arrested outside of Senator Shelley Moore Capito’s (R-WV) office in Morgantown for blocking access to the building, and they returned to the office on Tuesday.

item.title: Experts urge caution on betting as Super Bowl approaches
item.description: With the Super Bowl taking place this Sunday, sports betting activity is expected to rise, and experts are cautioning people to think twice before they make that bet.

item.title: West Virginia Senate honors victims of Agent Orange
item.description: CHARLESTON, W.Va. (WOWK) — The West Virginia Senate took time on Tuesday to recognize and honor victims of Agent Orange exposure during the Vietnam War. item.title: SILVER ALERT: State Police searching for missing West Virginia man
item.description: The West Virginia State Police has issued a Silver Alert for an elderly man missing out of Preston County.

item.title: WVDOT warns against driving with ice on your vehicle
item.description: As temperatures warm up a little bit, the West Virginia Department of Transportation (WVDOT) is warning drivers against driving with ice on their vehicles.

item.title: Vehicle found upside down in Harrison County creek
item.description: A vehicle was found on its top in a Harrison County creek early Tuesday morning.

item.title: Monongalia County sued over alleged assault in prisoner van
item.description: A Maryland woman has filed a lawsuit against the Monongalia County Commission, claiming she was physically and sexually assaulted by now-convicted murderer Jonathan Ramirez when they were both in county custody and being taken to the North Central Regional Jail.

item.title: Morgantown Raising Cane's opens to enthusiastic crowd
item.description: Following a soft grand opening on Monday, Raising Cane's celebrated the official grand opening of its first West Virginia location in Morgantown on Tuesday.

item.title: Where is West Virginia mentioned in the Epstein files?
item.description: Last week's sudden release of the Epstein files prompted many to dig in searching for names of celebrities, executives and other people of interest, but there's one subject that appears several hundred times—West Virginia.

item.title: Hearing held for West Virginia pastor accused of sexually abusing girls for years
item.description: Tuesday marked the first hearing in Lewis County court for John Radcliff, a former pastor accused of sexually abusing young girls over a period of several years.
